Worth paying attention to the onchain mechanism design here

The resolution fee scales with 7-day exit pressure. In quiet periods the fee is low, but as more holders rush for the exit it rises non-linearly until it hits a ceiling

50% of every fee is burned, while the other 50% is redistributed to the bankers who stayed

That makes selling into stress progressively more expensive while directly rewarding longer hold times and those willing to absorb the exit pressure

It effectively turns a “bank run” from a race to the exit into an economic trade-off, with the incentive dynamically adjusting to actual behaviour rather than relying on a fixed lockup or static exit tax

It’s onchain experimentation season, all taking place on Robinhood chain

Pay attention

The 5-year/5-year forward TIPS inflation breakeven rate is the 5-year average annual inflation rate over the next five years (the residual from the 10-year and 5-year TIPS inflation breakeven rates). So, it is what the market is expecting the inflation rate to average between 2031 and 2036.

The expectation is that the inflation rate over the next decade will settle back toward the post-GFC rate.
----
But for the next five years, inflation is expected to remain elevated. It is not expected to rage out of control, but to be higher than the Fed’s 2% target, probably somewhere between 3% and 4%.

Typical inflation cycles last around 10 years (8 to 12 years), so this is perfectly consistent with history: we have another 5 years or so of elevated inflation before this cycle ends.
